module_title: Preamble and Salient Features - Basic Understanding
introduction: The Indian Constitution is a unique document. It begins with a 'Preamble', which acts as an introduction or 'identity card' of the Constitution, setting out its main goals and philosophy. The Constitution itself has several standout features that distinguish it from other constitutions around the world.

core_concepts.title: The Preamble
core_concepts.description: It starts with 'We, the People of India...', showing that the ultimate power lies with the citizens. It declares India to be a Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic, and Republic state.

core_concepts.title: Longest Written Constitution
core_concepts.description: India has the lengthiest written constitution in the world. Originally (in 1949), it contained a Preamble, 395 Articles, 22 Parts, and 8 Schedules. (Currently, it has 12 Schedules).

core_concepts.title: Parliamentary Form of Government
core_concepts.description: Borrowed from the UK, India has a parliamentary system where the President is the nominal head (titular executive) and the Prime Minister is the real head (real executive). The executive is responsible to the legislature.

core_concepts.title: Meaning of Key Words
core_concepts.description: Sovereign: Independent country. Socialist: Welfare of the people. Secular: State has no official religion. Democratic: Government elected by the people. Republic: Head of state (President) is elected, not a king/queen.

important_entities.name: N.A. Palkhivala
important_entities.significance: He famously referred to the Preamble as the 'Identity Card of the Constitution'.

important_entities.name: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
important_entities.significance: He defended the voluminous nature of the Constitution by stating it was necessary to include administrative details to avoid future constitutional breakdowns.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: No. A common mistake is thinking you can go to court if the ideals in the Preamble are not met. The Preamble is 'non-justiciable', meaning its provisions are not enforceable in courts of law.

mnemonics_and_tricks.trick_title: Order of Words in the Preamble
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic, Republic. Memorize this exact sequence as it is frequently asked in basic objective exams.

exam_strategy_tips: Remember the original numbers: 395 Articles and 8 Schedules. Currently, there are 12 Schedules.
Questions directly asking what 'Republic' means (elected head of state) are very common.
